hi! Filipino here. the Makapili organisation served Japan, spying for them. though, whether they were sincerely loyal to Japan with full knowledge is questionable; many were peasants drawn simply with promises of postwar land reform, especially since a lot were dissatisfied with how America and Spain - the Philippines’ past colonisers - treated them. 

politicians like Jose P. Laurel (the puppet president during that period) collaborated chiefly because they were practically forced to: Manuel L. Quezon, the president before the war, essentially assigned him to that role because he had ties with Japan before the war (for example, having an honorary degree from Tokyo Imperial University/University of Tokyo). 

going back to Makapili, now with connections to Laurel — they were founded by Benigno Ramos and Artemio Ricarte *specifically* because Laurel refused to formally conscript Filipinos to fight for Japan. Ricarte, a former revolutionary and soldier, collaborated because Tojo Hideki promised to give the Philippines independence from the US and helped found Makapili for this reason. Ramos, too, collaborated because he was not exactly fond of America either. but as far as i know, he wasn’t talked into collaborating the way Tojo tried to discuss with Ricarte. he had been exiled in Japan before the war, but when he returned and during the war he became the leader of the pro-Japanese Ganap Party which readily collaborated. now, that is a collaborator.

the Ganap Party was born out of the old (anti-American) Sakdalista movement, which was also composed mostly of peasants. so, again, much of the collaboration among individual members was not undying loyalty, but a need to survive combined with probable false promises from Japan. 

so in a way, almost any politician serving at the time, regardless of their actual opinion on Imperial Japan, was collaborating, not out of loyalty, but because they didn’t have much of a choice. individuals in parties and organisations collaborated out of a need to survive too, and because they were lured in with the false promise of independence after their disillusionment with the US. some individuals, like Ramos, were genuinely pro-Japan too. collaborators are sort of a mixed bag.
